items.rootCause: The app cancelled the search itself, from the old React root's MatchScreen unmount cleanup. That cleanup skips match.cancel() only when useRootTeardown() reports a teardown (loop 9). The check had two signals: a newer root has mounted, or AppState is 'background' or 'inactive'. Both lose a race on a real recreation. Android pauses, destroys and creates the activity in one go on its main thread. Fabric's stopSurface is updateContainer(null) (ReactFabric-prod.js), so React unmounts the old tree in a scheduled render, not at once. By the time the old cleanups ran, the new activity's onHostResume had already set AppState back to 'active', and the new root had not mounted yet. So tornDown() was false and match.cancel() went out, and the server removed the queue entry. Phone 1 then got a bot. The store's search was now 'cancelled', so liveFlowPathOf returned null and the new root stayed on Home. A running game survives the same change because nothing in its unmount ends it, and resumeAtStart rejoins it. The swipe from Recents is already handled on the server: a search is not held for reconnection, so the dropped socket's onLeave calls service.left(), which drops the entry. I confirmed this over the real wire.
items.fix: apps/mobile/src/services/latestRoot.tsx: LatestRootOnly now has an effect whose cleanup adds its root to a `going` set. React runs a removed tree's passive cleanups top-down (commitPassiveUnmountEffectsInsideOfDeletedTree_begin is pre-order), so this runs before any screen's cleanup in that root. useRootTeardown() now also returns true when its own root is in `going`. A player never unmounts a whole root, so this signal never fires on a real leave and does not depend on timing. The effect clears its mark when it runs again, so React's strict mode in development does no harm. resetLatestRootForTests also clears the set. The friends room lobby uses the same hook, so it gets the same protection during a recreation. apps/mobile/src/screens/match/MatchScreen.tsx: a module-level registry counts the MatchScreens that show each search. When the screen goes with its root, the search is not cancelled at once. If no MatchScreen shows that search again within SEARCH_REOPEN_MS (6 s), the search is cancelled after all. That covers a task removed while the process stays alive, or a new root that went somewhere else. No search is left running that nobody sees. A real leave with the app in front is unchanged: the cancel goes out a beat later. The swipe kill keeps its existing behaviour: the process dies, the socket closes and the server drops the entry. The account can search again at once (no alreadyQueued), and the reopened app starts on Home with nothing stuck. No strings and no animations changed.
items.test: apps/mobile/src/screens/match/__tests__/MatchScreen.test.tsx, new describe 'the search through a recreated activity'. It uses the real MatchScreen inside latestRootOnly, over a real MatchmakingClient and FakeMatchmaking. (1) The old root is unmounted while AppState is not 'background' and no newer root exists, which is the device's real ordering. Nothing is sent and the phase stays 'searching'. The new root shows the same search, and after SEARCH_REOPEN_MS + 1 s it still runs. 'ביטול חיפוש' there still sends cancel. (2) The root goes and the new root shows something else: nothing is sent before 6 s, then cancel is sent and the phase is 'cancelled'. With the going check disabled, both tests fail (cancel sent at once); I restored it after. apps/server/test/matchmaking.test.ts, new test 'the app killed while searching (swiped from Recents)', over the real wire: a leave(false) mid-search, then the next searcher sees nextRange null and a timeout with no 'found', and the killed account's new search is accepted. This one passes on the existing code; it covers the behaviour I chose rather than a code change. Also passing: 77 mobile suites (1134 tests), among them the net, match, friends, services, game, recreatedRootResume, rankedResume e2e, ranked e2e, startupGraph and latestRoot suites. The server matchmaking suite passes 12 of 12. tsc passes for mobile and server, eslint is clean, prettier was run, and all files use LF.

items.rootCause: Confirmed by a test. Loop 10's GameRoom.welcomeBack sends `countdown` and then `lobby` to a connection that comes back during 3-2-1, before there is any state. RemoteGameHost's lobby handler, when state is null, always took the 'back in a lobby after a drop' path: it set lost = null and comingBack = null and set status to 'lobby'. A token reconnect during the count therefore ended the return early. At GO, onSnapshot saw lost === null: no hard/soft decision, no resyncedAt (the 'back, all synced' banner), and comingBack was null, so no 'reconnect' telemetry and no metrics.cameBack. The status also jumped from 'reconnecting' to 'lobby' in the middle of the count.
items.fix: Client only, in apps/mobile/src/net/remoteGameHost.ts, in the lobby case. A lobby that arrives while a return is under way (lost !== null) and a count is running (startsAt !== null) now only stores the lobby and calls notifyOnline. lost and comingBack stay as they are, so the snapshot at GO ends the return exactly as before loop 10. The returning player still gets the profiles (avatar, flag) from that lobby. A lobby after a drop with no count (a friends lobby rejoined by code) and a fresh join are unchanged. The server is unchanged and keeps its order (countdown, then lobby), so all apps keep getting the profiles. Older apps, which still take the reset path, lose only the banner and telemetry of a reconnect that happened during the 3-second count. The drop is that short, so this is almost always a soft return anyway. Test fake, apps/mobile/src/net/testing/fakeServer.ts: a countdown(startsAt) method; welcomeBack during the count mirrors GameRoom (countdown then lobby); a drop during the count holds the seat for its token; lobby() takes LobbyPlayer[].
items.test: New test in apps/mobile/src/net/__tests__/remoteGameHost.test.ts: 'a drop in the 3… 2… 1…: back with the token; the lobby that comes with the count brings the cards, and the return still ends at GO'. Join, lobby with two cards (avatar and flag), countdown, cutMe, and the token reconnect gets countdown plus lobby. Then: lobby.players carries the cards, startsAt is kept, the status is still 'reconnecting' with reconnect.resyncing true, and nothing has been reset. At GO the snapshot gives status 'live', resyncedAt is set, and 'reconnect' {success:true, phase:'hard'} is tracked. On the old code it fails with Expected 'reconnecting', Received 'lobby' (checked by disabling the new branch, then restored). The remoteGameHost, friendsHost, friends, matchmaking, rejoinCards, FriendsRoomScreen and friendsRoutes suites pass.

The fix for item 1 rests on React's top-down order of passive cleanups in a deleted tree. That order is in the bundled ReactFabric renderer, and the test exercises the same reconciler. SEARCH_REOPEN_MS (6 s) is the longest a recreated root may take to show the search again before the search is let go. If the A16 ever takes longer, the new root's search screen will show 'cancelled' and go back. Risk: it is a module constant in MatchScreen.tsx, easy to raise. When the app is swiped away, Android normally kills the process. The server then drops the entry when the socket closes, which the server test checks. The 6-second guard matters only when the process outlives its task. The friends room lobby uses the same useRootTeardown and now survives a recreation too. issues.problem: Item 1: the 6 s SEARCH_REOPEN_MS fallback does not fire on Android while no activity is resumed. The report says it covers 'a task removed while the process stays alive', and on the phone that is overstated. React Native's JavaTimerManager pauses every JS timer between onHostPause and onHostResume. If the task is swiped away and the process survives, the setTimeout from goneWithRoot only fires on the next resume. Until then the queue entry stays on the server, kept alive by the native WebSocket ping, and another player can be matched with the invisible app. This is no regression: before the fix, the AppState-'background' teardown skipped the cancel forever. When the app is reopened, the overdue timer fires at onHostResume, usually before the new root's MatchScreen mounts, so the app lands on Home with nothing stuck. The usual swipe kills the process, and the server then drops the entry, as the new server test shows.
issues.evidence: node_modules/react-native/ReactAndroid/src/main/java/com/facebook/react/modules/core/JavaTimerManager.kt:72-88: onHostPause sets isPaused=true and clears the frame callback. The TimerFrameCallback returns early while isPaused (lines 291-293). MatchScreen.tsx goneWithRoot uses a plain setTimeout(…, SEARCH_REOPEN_MS). The MatchScreen test 'the root went and no screen shows the search again' runs on a manual scheduler, so it never models paused timers.
issues.suggestion: No change is needed for the density bug. Correct the claim in the handoff notes: a process that outlives its swiped task keeps its search until the app is reopened or the process dies. In device check D, if Phone 1 does get matched with the swiped Phone 3, first check whether Phone 3's process survived (adb shell pidof). If that case must be closed, it needs a server-side or native signal, such as the server dropping a search whose client has not sent an app-level heartbeat. A JS timer cannot do it.

issues.problem: Item 1 rests on React running a deleted tree's passive-effect cleanups top-down. That holds in the bundled renderer. The diagnosis (AppState back to 'active' before the old surface's unmount, and no newer root yet) was reasoned out, not seen in a device log, so the fix needs the phone check to confirm it.
issues.evidence: node_modules/react-native/Libraries/Renderer/implementations/ReactFabric-prod.js:8808 commitPassiveUnmountEffectsInsideOfDeletedTree_begin unmounts a fiber's hooks (tag 0/11/15) and then descends to fiber.child, so it is pre-order. LatestRootOnly is the component registered in apps/mobile/index.ts (renderRootComponent(latestRootOnly(App))). Its cleanup therefore runs going.add(order) before MatchScreen's cleanup. The ordering is sound. The other ways this could fail are ruled out: the WebSocket survives a recreation (a running game survives it), and nothing else in the new root clears the store.
issues.suggestion: Run device steps A to C as listed. If the search still drops, take a logcat with the matchmaking client log ('cancel') to see whether the cancel comes from MatchScreen or from somewhere else.

issues.problem: Item 2 compatibility with old apps: an old app on the loop-10 server still takes the reset path when the lobby arrives during 3-2-1. For a reconnect that happens during the count, it loses the 'back, synced' banner, the hard/soft decision and the reconnect telemetry. The report states this openly. The gameplay is unaffected: the snapshot at GO still sets the status to 'live'.
issues.evidence: apps/server/src/rooms/GameRoom.ts:1053-1058 welcomeBack sends sendCountdown and then sendLobbyTo in the countdown phase. The old client's lobby handler with state null sets lost=null and comingBack=null and the status to 'lobby'. The new client branch (remoteGameHost.ts:813) keeps the return open. The countdown cannot go back to the lobby on the server: countDown and onMatchCountdown only move from lobby to countdown, and onMatchCancel goes to over. startsAt is never reset in the host, and a host is not reused after a game, so the new branch cannot catch a real 'back in a lobby'.
issues.suggestion: No change is needed. Accept it as documented.

issues.problem: A pre-existing console.error appears in the MatchScreen suite: 'An update to FlowFallback inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)'. It comes from an older test (the show() helper at MatchScreen.test.tsx:336), not from the new describe. It is noise only.
issues.evidence: npx jest src/screens/match/__tests__/MatchScreen.test.tsx passes and prints console.error with FlowFallback, stack at MatchScreen.test.tsx:336 (show).
issues.suggestion: Optional: wrap that helper's state change in act().

items.rootCause: Not found off the device, so no code change. What the evidence shows: (1) The empty frame f71 is a single colour, exactly #0f1218 (color.bg), on every pixel except the status-bar icons. There are no wandering digits in it. On phone 1 the digits normally do show in screencaps (for example RF8Y60PP2XZ-pregame-found-rematch-now.png). (2) The ambient digits are an opaque Skia canvas, which on Android is a SurfaceView. It sits outside the navigator (app/_layout.tsx AmbientLayer). So this is not 'the stack had no fragment for a frame': that frame would still show the digits. In f71 neither the ambient SurfaceView nor any screen was drawn, only the root's or window's bg. (3) In the montage fix10-RF8Y60PP2XZ-fullboard-rm-1.png the empty tile is 5th of the 6 'before' tiles, and the 6th is the full board again. So the order reads board, EMPTY, board, results, not a blank during the push. (4) Under Reduced Motion the native stack transition is the same (flow = 'fade'; Android always runs its own 150 ms). The only RM-specific differences on this path are in JS: the full-board hold is reducedFade (200 ms) instead of 1100 ms; the score delta and lead cue happen at once; and the ambient is AmbientStill, one picture drawn once. Ruled out by reading the code: Modals (all transparent and nav-translucent, and none opens at the end), the Splash (it has content), FlowFallback (it has text), the ConnectionLayer (its model is NONE once the view is over), the match entry being dropped, keep-awake, and system-bar changes (no JS touches them). The one code path that fits both 'everything including the ambient gone for one commit' and 'board again afterwards' is a root swap (services/latestRoot.tsx: after an activity recreation 'the newest root is empty for that one commit'). After it the GameScreen remounts on an over view and opens the results through 'game over on arrival'. But nothing I found recreates the activity at the end of a game, so this is a hypothesis to check on the phone, not a cause.
items.fix: None for this item in this round. I did not ship a speculative change: lengthening the Reduced-Motion full-board hold would change motion.md game.end / last.cell without a demonstrated mechanism, and a different native race would not be fixed by it.
items.test: None. No mechanism I could reproduce under Jest. The loop-9 regression (resultsHandoff.test.tsx: the first commit of the results is the hero, Reduced Motion off and on) still covers the push itself.
items.deviceCheck: Phone 1, in-app Reduced Motion ON, Hebrew, ranked fast vs the stealth bot; let the bot fill the last cell. Use 'adb shell screenrecord --bit-rate 20000000' (not screencap, which samples) and, in parallel, 'adb logcat -v time ActivityTaskManager:I ActivityManager:I ReactNative:V ReactNativeJS:V SurfaceView:V *:S'. Repeat 6 times. For each run, report: (a) whether an all-#0f1218 frame (no digits) appears, and whether a board frame follows it before the results; (b) whether logcat shows any 'Relaunch'/'recreate'/configuration change, or a SurfaceView surfaceDestroyed/surfaceCreated, in the same second; (c) the same with Reduced Motion OFF (2 runs). If (b) shows a recreation or a SurfaceView surface cycle at that moment, send the log lines: that names the layer, and the fix follows.

items.rootCause: The picker's boxes were fixed at the design's text size, but React Native grows the text and its lineHeight with the system font scale. (1) A kind's name had a View of exactly 2 × 16 dp (2 design lines). At 1.3 its two lines draw 2 × 20.8 dp, so the second line ('digits', 'keypad') ran under the price chip. (2) The info line was numberOfLines={1}, so at 1.3 it ended in '…'. (3) In '· Next: {{cost}}' a plain space separates the word from the number, so the wrapping words broke as 'Next:' over '4'. pickerLayout's every-kind-fits proof also used the design sizes only.
items.fix: metrics.ts: arsenalMetricsFor(typeface, fontScale) gives the picker's words a growth textGrowth(fontScale), from 1 up to PICKER_FONT_CAP = FONT_SCALE_CAPS.hud (1.35); a smaller system text keeps the design's boxes. The boxes grow with it: button.nameBox (2 lines × lineHeight × growth), the button height, price.height (two grown label lines), and the info line (2 lines when grown). New fields: textScale, button.nameBox, info.line / info.lines. At scale 1 everything equals the old values (he/en test unchanged). The fixer's analysis is honest, but it skips one lead that is specific to Reduced Motion. Under RM the ambient layer is AmbientStill (AmbientCanvas.tsx:141-153): an opaque Skia Canvas, which is a SurfaceView on Android, recorded once and never redrawn by a clock. AmbientLive redraws every frame through useFrameCallback, so if its surface is re-created or arrives late, the next frame covers it. AmbientStill has nothing that would. A frame where the screens are briefly not drawn (loop 7 already saw 'only the digits' frames during stack changes) and the ambient surface has no buffer would show exactly what f71 shows: the GestureHandlerRootView background, color.bg #0f1218 (app/_layout.tsx:75), with no digits and no content. That explains 'RM on only' better than the root-swap hypothesis. A second candidate the fixer did not look at: dropWhenCovered's CommonActions.reset removes the game route under the results, and react-native-screens may detach and re-attach fragments while doing it. That could explain 'board, EMPTY, board'.

items.rootCause: Still not found off the device. I checked both new leads from the review and the code rules them out. (1) The idea that 'AmbientStill has nothing that redraws it': under RM the opaque Canvas is a SkiaSurfaceView (SkiaBaseView.setOpaque). When a surface is re-created, RNSkAndroidView.surfaceAvailable calls RNSkView::redraw() right away, and surfaceSizeChanged does too (react-native-skia 2.6.2, android/cpp/rnskia-android/RNSkAndroidView.h:37-56). So a re-created surface gets the still picture without any frame clock, and AmbientStill is not worse off than AmbientLive there. (2) dropWhenCovered's CommonActions.reset: it runs only once the game route is no longer the one shown (transitionEnd closing, or the 600 ms fallback), so the results are already on top. The montage fix10-RF8Y60PP2XZ-fullboard-rm-1.png (I looked at it) shows board, board, board, board, EMPTY, board, then results. The blank falls between two board frames, before any results frame, so the reset cannot be the cause. Also, the same openResults → push → dropWhenCovered path runs for surrender and 'סיום אימון', and those were clean 14 times. What is left: a window- or root-level event during the full-board hold, before the push. Under RM that hold is 200 ms, not 1100 ms. (1) The idea that 'AmbientStill has nothing that redraws it': under RM the opaque Canvas is a SkiaSurfaceView (SkiaBaseView.setOpaque). When a surface is re-created, RNSkAndroidView.surfaceAvailable calls RNSkView::redraw() right away, and surfaceSizeChanged does too (react-native-skia 2.6.2, android/cpp/rnskia-android/RNSkAndroidView.h:37-56). So a re-created surface gets the still picture without any frame clock, and AmbientStill is not worse off than AmbientLive there. (2) dropWhenCovered's CommonActions.reset: it runs only once the game route is no longer the one shown (transitionEnd closing, or the 600 ms fallback), so the results are already on top. The montage fix10-RF8Y60PP2XZ-fullboard-rm-1.png (I looked at it) shows board, board, board, board, EMPTY, board, then results. The blank falls between two board frames, before any results frame, so the reset cannot be the cause. Also, the same openResults → push → dropWhenCovered path runs for surrender and 'סיום אימון', and those were clean 14 times. What is left: a window- or root-level event during the full-board hold, before the push. Under RM that hold is 200 ms, not 1100 ms. It is a single frame in 1 of 4 runs, and the RM-off sample is only 2 runs, so it may not be RM-specific at all.
items.fix: No code change, on purpose. Neither lead holds up, and a speculative change (a longer RM hold, a non-opaque ambient) would change motion.md or performance without a demonstrated cause.

For each run, report: (a) whether a frame of plain #0f1218 appears (no board, no results), its time from the last cell, and whether a board frame follows it before the results; (b) any log lines in that second: SurfaceView surfaceDestroyed/surfaceCreated, 'SkiaView onSurfaceTextureSizeChanged', a Relaunch or configuration change, a window add or remove (a Modal or Dialog closing); (c) whether any sheet or menu was open on the game screen when the bot finished. Send the log lines around any blank frame. If the blank shows up with RM off too, the item is not RM-specific.

items.rootCause: (1) The picker's boxes stayed at the design's sizes, while Android grows the text and its lineHeight with font_scale. The name box was 2×16 dp, so the second line went under the chip. The info line was numberOfLines 1, so it ended in '…'. (2) '· Next: 4' sat in a narrow share of a single price row and wrapped at a space. A no-break space before the number alone (round 1) was not enough. With the whole piece glued, it is wider than that share in many languages at 1.3 (en, he, ar, de, fr, ...) and even at 1.0 (de, it, pl). Fabric's TextLayoutManager ignores minimumFontScale: it floors only at the native minimumFontSize, which is not even in Text's validAttributes, so JS cannot pass it, and otherwise at 4 dp. So the glued piece would have shrunk below the design size on the phone.
items.fix: Round 1 kept: growth up to FONT_SCALE_CAPS.hud (1.35) for the names, the info line (2 lines) and the button heights. fittedPicker lowers the growth until every kind fits at once. New this round: (a) metrics.ts: with a grown text (textScale > 1), price.stacked is true and the price row puts its two halves on two lines: 'Price −2 pts · Next: 4' on the first, 'Your score 6 → 4' on the second, at the end side. Its height is hairlines + 2×paddingY(6) + rowGap(4) + ceil(grow×(max(Teko30 line, label line) + max(Teko22 line, label line))). fittedPicker counts that height, so every kind still fits at once. At the design size the row is exactly as before (one line of 48, flexDirection row). (b) wording.ts nextPriceText: any space next to something that is not a letter becomes U+00A0. In English that gives '· Next: 4', one piece, so neither the number nor the bullet can stand alone on a line, and French ' :' stays joined. A space between two words still breaks (vi 'Tiếp theo'). PriceRow uses it only when stacked. At the design size it shows t('arsenal.nextPrice') unchanged. (c) The design-size boxes are no longer rounded: grown() applies Math.ceil only when grow > 1 (nameBox, info.height), so they equal the design's exactly. (d) The comments now say the floor on Android is the measured fit (the search keeps the largest size that fits), not minimumFontScale. No locale strings changed.
items.test: pickerFits.test.ts: lineCount now breaks only at breakable spaces and treats U+00A0 as joining, with the words measured as drawn. wrapsIn takes minScale and a line count. The new helper priceRowFits models the real row at m.textScale: every text grown, the shared line at 1.0, and the stacked lines when grown. New per-language test at 1.3 on the 360×780, 360×640 and 390×844 phones, using fittedPicker's metrics: nextPriceText's piece and 'Your score' (plus 'missing') each fit their one line at the grown size, or shrunk to the design size and no lower. It passes in all 19 languages and the pseudo locales; es and pt-BR, cut today in the shared line, now fit. New test: the stacked row's height holds both grown lines, and it is not stacked at 1.0. nextPriceText test: the text is unchanged once U+00A0 is drawn as a space; a breakable space only between two letters; never '· ' or a space before the number; exact en/fr/vi results. ArsenalOverlay.test.tsx: the 1.3 test (Dimensions 360×780, fontScale 1.3) now also checks that arsenal-next is '· Next: 4', the price row is flexDirection column with the grown height (> 48), and arsenal-after has alignSelf flex-end. The B45 test now renders at fontScale 1 via setWindow(PHONE) (Jest's default window has fontScale 2), and checks that the row is still one 48-dp row with no U+00A0. The new 1.3 assertions fail on round 1's code (no stacking, no bullet glue), and the price-row fit test failed for 21 language/phone cases before stacking. Results: 1361 tests in 43 suites pass (arsenal/*, hit/*, levels/*, widthBudget, GameScreenDuel, GameScreenHit). tsc clean, eslint clean, prettier applied, no CR in any changed file.

items.rootCause: Already fixed in loop 10's rework, and the reviewer confirmed it. In Warp.tsx, `active` is true only for a running 'warp' hit in the frame's own region. An inactive frame gets an idle clock and returns the cached STRAIGHT style before it reads the clock. So during fireworks, cats, ink, scramble or keypad, nothing is sent to the native views on each frame. During a warp, the frame in scope moves on the shared clock, so the dim and the overlay start in the same frame.
items.fix: No change. The code is unchanged since snap-loop11.

final.notes:
How each review issue was handled. Medium #1 (item 1): it stays partial, not fixed. Both suggested leads are refuted with evidence (Skia redraws on surfaceAvailable; the drop runs only after the results are on top, while the blank comes between two board frames). The device check is extended: screenrecord, logcat tags including SurfaceView and SkiaView, RM on and off with 6 runs each, and whether a sheet or menu was open. Medium #2 (item 2): confirmed. Fabric ignores minimumFontScale, and minimumFontSize is not in Text's validAttributes, so it cannot be passed from JS. Gluing '· Next: 4' into the shared row would have shrunk it below the design size in many languages. Fix: with a grown text the price row stacks its halves on two lines, so the glued piece has the row's width. The fit tests now measure the real nextPriceText string (U+00A0 joins) at 1.0 and at the fitted textScale, on every phone of 360 dp or more, in all 19 languages. At font_scale 1.0 the row and its text are exactly as before. Low #3: ceil only when grown, and the comments say the floor on Android is the measured fit. Low #4: noted below.

Checks: tsc -p apps/mobile clean. eslint clean on all changed files. prettier --write only on the files I changed. No CR in any of them. Jest: 1361 tests in 43 suites pass. No locale strings changed, so the i18n check was not needed. No adb, build, deploy or install.

Design note for Moshe or the design doc: at a large system text (font_scale > 1) the picker's price row is now two lines (price and next on the first, my score on the second). components.md §13 describes only the 48-dp single row.

The app's 'פרק 2 נעול: צריך 20 כוכבים בפרק 1. יש לך 6.' follows it except that it leaves out 'חסרים N' (he/levels.json lockedGate_*). The catalog's 'פרק 2 נפתח ב־20 כוכבים בפרק 1' matches neither, so the app text is kept and the catalog should change.
